question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

? , 637, 629, 621, 613, 605, 597, 589
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 645.

GIVEN

• ? , 637, 629, 621, 613, 605, 597, 589

SOLUTION

• The series decreases by a constant 8: 637−8=629, 629−8=621, 621−8=613, and so on.

• So the missing first term = 637 + 8 = 645.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Common difference is −8; move one step left of 637 → add 8 → 645.

NOTE

• In an arithmetic series with common difference d, the term before the first known term = first term − d (here d = −8, so add 8).

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

OZL : RCO :: BTU : EWX :: AHX : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. DKA.

GIVEN

• OZL : RCO :: BTU : EWX :: AHX : ?

SOLUTION

• Each letter of the cluster moves forward by +3.

• OZL → O+3=R, Z+3=C, L+3=O → RCO ✓; BTU → E,W,X ✓.

• AHX → A+3=D, H+3=K, X+3=A (X=24, 24+3=27→A) = DKA.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Add 3 to every letter; wrap Z→C, X→A (mod 26).

NOTE

• Use A=1…Z=26; for letters past Z subtract 26 to wrap around.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

MN, II, ED, AY, WT, SO, OJ, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. KE.

GIVEN

• MN, II, ED, AY, WT, SO, OJ, ?

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: M(13), I(9), E(5), A(1), W(23), S(19), O(15), ? → each −4 → 15−4=11 = K.

• 2nd letters: N(14), I(9), D(4), Y(25), T(20), O(15), J(10), ? → each −5 → 10−5=5 = E.

• So missing term = KE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• First letters step back 4, second letters step back 5 (wrap mod 26).

NOTE

• Split each cluster into positions and find separate patterns for column-1 and column-2.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(KR, HK, ED)

(DE, AX, XQ)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (JH, GA, DT).

GIVEN

• (KR, HK, ED) and (DE, AX, XQ)

SOLUTION

• Rule: across the three clusters, the 1st letters fall by 3 and the 2nd letters fall by 7 (mod 26).

• Check (KR,HK,ED): K(11)→H(8)→E(5) (−3); R(18)→K(11)→D(4) (−7). ✓

• Option 1 (JH,GA,DT): J(10)→G(7)→D(4) (−3); H(8)→A(1)→T(20) (−7, since 1−7=−6→20). ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• First letters −3 each, second letters −7 each; only Option 1 fits both.

NOTE

• For sets of three clusters, test the step between consecutive clusters column-wise.

question: 13th of a month is Wednesday. This month has 28 days. What will be the 28th of next month?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Thursday.

GIVEN

• 13th = Wednesday; this month has 28 days.

SOLUTION

• 13th Wed → 20th Wed → 27th Wed, so 28th (last day) = Thursday.

• Next month 1st = Friday. Then 1,8,15,22 = Friday; 28th = 22nd + 6 days = Friday + 6 = Thursday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• 28 days = exactly 4 weeks, so days repeat. 28th of next month = same weekday as 28th of this month = Thursday.

NOTE

• Any block of 7 (or 28) days returns to the same weekday; use this to skip counting.

question: What was the first day of the year 1915?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Friday.

GIVEN

• Find the day on 1 January 1915.

SOLUTION

• Odd days up to 1914 years = 1600(0) + 300(1) + 14 years.

• 14 years (1601–1614) have 3 leap years → 11×1 + 3×2 = 17 → 17 mod 7 = 3 odd days.

• Total = 0 + 1 + 3 = 4 odd days (up to end of 1914). Adding 1 for Jan-1 → 5.

• 5 odd days = Friday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 0=Sun,1=Mon,…,5=Fri. Count odd days to the date and read off the day.

NOTE

• 100 yrs = 5 odd days, 200 = 3, 300 = 1, 400 = 0; ordinary year 1, leap year 2 odd days.

question: Height of 5 trapezium A, B, C, D and E is compared. Height of no two trapezium is same. Height of E is maximum. Height of C is less than D but more than B. Height of A is not more than B. Height of which trapezium is minimum?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A.

GIVEN

• E is maximum; B < C < D; A ≤ B (and no two equal, so A < B).

SOLUTION

• Combining: A < B < C < D < E.

• The smallest height therefore belongs to A.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Chain the inequalities into one line A<B<C<D<E; the left end is the minimum.

NOTE

• In order/ranking, convert each statement to a single symbol chain to read max and min directly.

question: 7 children P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). V is second to the right of R. S and T are next to each other. S is not the immediate neighbour of R or V. Q is third to the left of P. T is third to the right of U. Q is the immediate neighbour of T. Considering towards right of R, who is sitting between R and V?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. U.

GIVEN

• 7 seats, facing centre. V is 2nd to right of R; T is 3rd to right of U; Q is immediate neighbour of T; Q is 3rd to left of P; S–T adjacent; S not next to R or V.

SOLUTION

• Fix R, and go right (clockwise): R, _, V occupy R, seat+1, seat+2.

• Placing U at seat+1 gives T at seat+4 (3rd to right of U); then Q at seat+3 (neighbour of T) and P at seat+6 (Q 3rd to left of P); S at seat+5 and remaining P/S satisfy S not next to R or V.

• The seat between R and V (going right) is filled by U.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 'V second to right of R' leaves exactly one seat between them; testing 'T third right of U' forces U into that seat.

NOTE

• Facing centre: a person's right is the clockwise direction; anchor one fixed clue first.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. a square containing a circle and a square-in-square placed side by side.

GIVEN

• 1st figure: outer square → circle → pentagon (nested). 2nd figure: the inner two shapes (circle and pentagon) un-nested and placed side by side inside the square.

SOLUTION

• Rule: keep the outer square as a frame; take the shapes nested inside it and set them side by side.

• 3rd figure: outer square → circle → (square-in-square). So the answer = square holding a circle and a square-in-square side by side = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• 'Un-nest' the inner pair from the first figure into two side-by-side shapes; apply the same to the third figure.

NOTE

• In figure analogies, first state the transformation in words, then apply it exactly to the third figure.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the block  + + # / @ @ # / * *.

GIVEN

• A symbol grid transforms into a 3-row block by the same rule shown in the first pair; the third grid (@ # / * +) must transform likewise.

SOLUTION

• The required block is exactly: row-1 (+ + #), row-2 (@ @ #), row-3 (* *).

• Checking options: Option 2 wrongly adds a third * in the last row; Option 3 replaces + + by ÷ ×; Option 4 replaces the middle-right # by −.

• Only Option keeps every cell as required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Derive the target grid once, then eliminate any option that differs in even a single cell — three options each change exactly one symbol.

NOTE

• For symbol-matrix questions, compare the options cell-by-cell against the pattern; the odd cell exposes the wrong option.

question:
Select the option that is related to the second number in the same way as the third number is related to the fourth number and fifth number is related to sixth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

? : 7119 :: 5743 : 5774 :: 2343 : 2374
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 7088.

GIVEN

• ? : 7119 :: 5743 : 5774 :: 2343 : 2374

SOLUTION

• In each pair the second number = first + 31: 5743 + 31 = 5774; 2343 + 31 = 2374.

• So ? + 31 = 7119 → ? = 7119 − 31 = 7088.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Find the constant gap (31) from a complete pair, then subtract it from 7119.

NOTE

• When one side of the pair is missing, reverse the operation found from the other pairs.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first number in the same way as the fourth number is related to the third number and sixth number is related to fifth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

89 : ? :: 923 : 1150 :: 242 : 469
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 316.

GIVEN

• 89 : ? :: 923 : 1150 :: 242 : 469

SOLUTION

• In each pair the second number = first + 227: 923 + 227 = 1150; 242 + 227 = 469.

• So ? = 89 + 227 = 316.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Read the constant addition (227) from a known pair and add it to 89.

NOTE

• Operate on the whole number as instructed; look for a common +k or ×k across all pairs.

question: In a certain code language, 'RIDE' is coded as '37' and 'BIKE' is coded as '28'. How will 'WATCH' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 56.

GIVEN

• RIDE = 37, BIKE = 28.

SOLUTION

• Add letter positions, then +1: RIDE = 18+9+4+5 = 36, 36+1 = 37 ✓; BIKE = 2+9+11+5 = 27, 27+1 = 28 ✓.

• WATCH = 23+1+20+3+8 = 55, 55 + 1 = 56.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Code = (sum of letter values) + 1.

NOTE

• Positions A=1…Z=26; test 'sum', 'sum±constant' or 'sum×k' on the given words first.

question: In a certain coded language 'WOMEN' is coded as 'XSKBJ' and 'UPSET' is coded as 'VTQBP'. How will 'FAZES' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. GEXBO.

GIVEN

• WOMEN = XSKBJ, UPSET = VTQBP.

SOLUTION

• Letter-wise shifts are +1, +4, −2, −3, −4: W+1=X, O+4=S, M−2=K, E−3=B, N−4=J ✓ (same for UPSET).

• FAZES → F+1=G, A+4=E, Z−2=X, E−3=B, S−4=O = GEXBO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Apply the fixed pattern +1, +4, −2, −3, −4 to the five letters in order.

NOTE

• Find the shift for each position from one clear example, then reuse it for the target word.

question: At what time (in PM), the angle between hour and minute hands of a clock will be 60 degrees?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 2:00.

GIVEN

• Find the time when the angle between the hands is 60°.

SOLUTION

• At 2:00 the minute hand is at 12 (0°) and the hour hand is at 2 → 2 × 30° = 60°.

• Angle = |60 − 0| = 60°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• On the hour H:00, angle = 30 × H (for H ≤ 6). 30 × 2 = 60°.

NOTE

• Angle formula: |30H − 5.5M| degrees, where H = hour, M = minutes.

question: A clock is 3 minutes fast at 11:30 AM and 9 minutes fast at 11:30 PM. At what time (in AM) will it show the correct time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 5:30.

GIVEN

• +3 min at 11:30 AM and +9 min at 11:30 PM (a 12-hour gap).

SOLUTION

• Gain in 12 hours = 9 − 3 = 6 min → rate = 0.5 min per hour.

• At 11:30 AM it is already +3 min fast; it was correct 3 ÷ 0.5 = 6 hours earlier.

• 11:30 AM − 6 hours = 5:30 AM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Correct time occurs error÷rate before the reference: 3 min ÷ 0.5 min/hr = 6 hr before 11:30 AM.

NOTE

• A uniformly gaining clock shows correct time only when its error is 0, i.e., just before it started gaining.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the star with the arrowhead pointing straight down and the tail on the lower-left arm.

GIVEN

• An eight-spoke star carrying a moving arrowhead and a short tail-bar on its arms.

SOLUTION

• As the series advances, the arrowhead rotates around the star and settles on the downward (south) arm, with the tail on the adjacent lower-left (south-west) arm.

• Among the options, only Option 4 shows the arrowhead pointing straight down with the tail on the south-west arm (Option 2 also points down but its tail is on the wrong arm).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Track just the arrowhead's rotation and then check the tail's arm to break the tie between the two 'down' options.

NOTE

• In figure series, follow one moving element at a time (here the arrowhead), then confirm secondary marks.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the box  hooked-line (top), down-arrow, up-arrow.

GIVEN

• Three items — an up-arrow (↑), a down-arrow (↓) and a hooked line — sit in the Left, Middle, Right positions of each box.

SOLUTION

• From each figure to the next, two items swap places, the swap cycling as (L↔R), (L↔M), (M↔R), …; and the hook flips between top and bottom every step.

• Figure 4 = (↑, ↓, hook-bottom). The next swap is (L↔R) giving (hook, ↓, ↑), and the hook flips to top → (hook-top, ↓, ↑) = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Apply the swap cycle L↔R, L↔M, M↔R repeatedly and remember to flip the hook each time.

NOTE

• When a fixed set of shapes only changes seats, look for a repeating cycle of pairwise swaps.

question: The ratio of present ages of two students is 8 : 7. The difference between their ages is 4 years. What is the age of the younger student?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 28 years.

GIVEN

• Ages ratio = 8 : 7; difference = 4 years.

SOLUTION

• Let ages be 8x and 7x. Difference = 8x − 7x = x = 4.

• Younger student = 7x = 7 × 4 = 28 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference of ratio parts = 1 part = 4 years; younger = 7 parts = 28.

NOTE

• In ratio problems, the value of one 'part' (x) unlocks every quantity.

question: The ratio of present ages of L and M is 6 : 9. L is 15 years younger than M. What will be the age of L after 26 years from present?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 56 years.

GIVEN

• L : M = 6 : 9; M − L = 15 years; find L's age after 26 years.

SOLUTION

• Let L = 6x, M = 9x. Difference = 9x − 6x = 3x = 15 → x = 5.

• Present L = 6x = 30 years. After 26 years = 30 + 26 = 56 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• 3 parts = 15 → 1 part = 5; L = 6 parts = 30, then add 26 = 56.

NOTE

• 'After n years' adds n to the present age of every person.
